conventions.convention: The HNN relation is oriented as t α(c) t^{-1}=β(c); in associated-subgroup notation C_-=α(C), C_+=β(C), and φ=β∘α^{-1}:C_-→C_+.
An HNN word has finite stable-letter length n≥0; its pins are tct^{-1} for c∈C_- and t^{-1}dt for d∈C_+.
The transversal data are explicitly the unique decompositions a=cs with c∈C_-, s∈S_- and a=dr with d∈C_+, r∈S_+; the initial coefficient is unrestricted.

A positive-length Britton-reduced word is cyclically Britton-reduced when the end rotation remains Britton-reduced; an end sign pattern (+,-) tests membership in C_- and (-,+) tests membership in C_+.
All simplicial paths are finite. A simplicial tree is nonempty, connected, and has no nontrivial reduced closed path.
An edge inversion means g(e)=bar(e); an action without inversions permits no such pair for any group element.
Translation length is the minimum of d_T(v,gv) over vertices, and is defined here for automorphisms acting without inversions.
Completely reducible means a finite direct sum of irreducible subrepresentations; the empty direct sum is allowed, so the zero representation is completely reducible.
The matrix-block, multiplicity, sum-of-squares, and irreducible-count conclusions assume G finite, k algebraically closed, and char(k) not dividing |G|.

Under the published category-theory size convention, a subobject is a mutual-factorisation class expressed by a formula, not a set-valued member of a gathered collection; an ordinary poset of representatives requires a supplied representative set.
The modular law is x∨(y∧z)=(x∨y)∧z only under the hypothesis x≤z.
A composition series is a finite strict chain 0=A_0<⋯<A_n=A with simple successive quotients; length is objectwise and includes the length-zero series of the zero object.
A generator is a single separating object; the canonical epimorphism from a coproduct of copies is an equivalent description only in the stated AB3 setting.
AB3/AB3* mean all small coproducts/products; AB4/AB4* add preservation of monomorphisms/epimorphisms; AB5/AB5* are the stated directed-join/decreasing-meet distributivity laws.

Arbitrary products of surjections in Ab, arbitrary coproducts of projectives, products of injectives, and the module-category enough-projectives assertion are explicitly choice-dependent; their finite versions are choice-free.

load_bearing.statement: An object G is a generator when the singleton {G} is separating; dually, Q is a cogenerator when {Q} is coseparating.
For groups A,C and injective α,β:C→A, the HNN extension is obtained by adjoining t with relations tα(c)t^{-1}=β(c) for every c∈C.

A tree automorphism without inversions has a minimum translation length and is exactly one of: elliptic with a fixed vertex and length 0, or hyperbolic with positive length and a unique invariant bi-infinite axis on which it translates by that length.
An element g inverts e when g(e)=bar(e); the action is without inversions when no oriented edge is inverted by any group element.
An HNN word is a_0t^{ε_1}a_1⋯t^{ε_n}a_n; pins are tct^{-1} with c∈C_- or t^{-1}dt with d∈C_+, and Britton-reduced words have no pins.

If a Britton-reduced HNN word represents the identity, then its stable-letter length is zero and its sole base coefficient is e_A; equivalently, every Britton-reduced word containing a stable letter is nontrivial.
If an object A has two composition series, the two series have the same length and the same composition factors up to permutation and isomorphism.
For P in an abelian category, projectivity, exactness of A(P,-) on every short exact sequence, and splitting of every epimorphism onto P are equivalent.
If G is finite and k is algebraically closed with char(k) not dividing |G|, then for a complete list V_i of irreducibles, ∑_i(dim_k V_i)^2=|G|.
For every object A of an abelian category, its subobjects form a bounded lattice: meet is pullback, join is the image construction, bottom is the zero subobject, and top is 1_A.
If G is finite and k is algebraically closed with char(k) not dividing |G|, then k[G]≅∏_{i=1}^r M_{n_i}(k) as k-algebras for positive integers n_i.
In an AB3 abelian category, G is a generator iff A(G,-) is faithful iff for every A the canonical coproduct map from copies of G indexed by A(G,A) to A is epic.

concerns.concern: The displayed ordinary presentation ⟨X,t | R, tα(c)t^{-1}=β(c)⟩ uses α(c),β(c) as elements of A=F(X)/⟨⟨R⟩⟩, whereas def-group-presentation requires relators to be words in the free group on X∪{t}. The definition needs chosen word representatives or an explicit relative-presentation convention.

The item calls S_± “left coset transversals” but writes C_±\A and the decompositions a=cs, which select representatives of cosets C_±s (right cosets under def-coset). The label and its asserted equivalent formulation point in opposite directions.

Step 2.1 asserts that forced front rewrites define an action of the presented HNN group but does not verify the HNN relators or construct an identification with the cited free product with amalgamation. The cited normal-form theorem is for a different construction, so uniqueness is not established by the proof as written.

The stated one-sided form is false with the transversal restriction given. For φ(n)=2n and S={0,1}, the element t^{-1}a^3t in BS(1,2) cannot be represented with the middle coefficient in S when both exponents are positive; the standard unique condition is that the middle coefficient lie outside φ(A), not that it be a fixed transversal representative.

The claimed odd-middle-coefficient normal form is plausible, but step 2.1 does not derive it from L2: membership in the nontrivial coset of 2Z means “odd,” whereas membership in the chosen transversal {0,1} means the single representative 1. The proof conflates a coset with its representative and relies on the defective preceding proposition.

Step 1.1 uses the false identity x^{-1}uxx^{-1}v^{-1}x=1. From x^{-1}ux=v one obtains x^{-1}uxv^{-1}=1; the displayed word instead simplifies to x^{-1}uv^{-1}x and need not be trivial. The minimal-conjugator argument therefore does not prove the lemma.

The definition calls d_T a metric, while its justified-by lemma proves only integer-valuedness and realization by the unique reduced path. Positivity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality are not stated or proved locally, though a reader can reconstruct them from unique-path cancellation.

Step 3.1 says that when the finite invariant subtree U⊂T' has odd diameter, the midpoint of a geometric edge of U is already a vertex of the once-subdivided tree T'. That is generally false for an edge of T'. The conclusion can be repaired quickly using the inversion-free action: a setwise-fixed center edge cannot have its endpoints swapped, so an endpoint is fixed.

The statement gathers “the subobjects of A” into a bounded lattice and later items write Sub(A), but the cited published convention def-subobject-and-quotient-object explicitly says subobjects are proper-class formulas, are never gathered into a collection, and yield an ordinary poset only after a representative set is supplied. No well-poweredness or representative set is assumed here, so the lattice is not type-correct under the library's own convention.

The statement assumes AB3 but not local smallness, yet condition 3 indexes a coproduct by A(G,A), and L3 applies only to locally small categories. Without local smallness that hom-collection need not be a set, so AB3 does not supply the displayed coproduct.

The item claims that a particular “chosen-well-powering branch” of the special adjoint functor theorem has all its hypotheses satisfied, but it cites no statement of that theorem or branch. L2 only defines well-poweredness; it does not state the branch's full hypotheses, so the SAFT conclusion cannot be checked from the supplied dependencies.

Step 1.1 proves the canonical map s:⊕X→∏X is epic, but step 2.1 immediately calls it an isomorphism. Monicity follows from AB5⇒AB4 by viewing s as a coproduct of the coordinate inclusions, but that theorem is neither cited nor invoked.

Step 2.1 invokes the canonical-coproduct characterization L2, whose theorem assumes AB3, although this statement assumes only an abelian category. The claim remains easy to prove directly from the separating definition of generator, but the cited route is outside its stated domain.

Step 1.1 says to use the inclusion Z→Z⊕Z/p to promote the generator property, but separating maps requires constructing a map from Z⊕Z/p to the source object. The correct quick argument uses the projection Z⊕Z/p→Z and then checks nonzeroness by composing back with the inclusion.

The computation derives irreducible degrees 1,1,2 and then cites only the bare existence of some matrix-block product to identify the block sizes. The cited statement does not say that its factors correspond to irreducibles with sizes equal to their degrees; the regular-representation multiplicity theorem or simple-module classification must be invoked. The same citation gap occurs in the C3 and Q8/Dih(C4) decomposition examples.
